item: Same pulses, new subdivision
content: The second half of a piece repeats the cycle and the melody of the first half with a different subdivision of the same pulses. The listener hears a new metre, but the long and short pulses do not change.
parameters: Long pulse: 3 eighths, then 5 notes. Short pulse: 2 eighths, then 3 notes

item: Expansion of the basic pattern
content: The bridge takes the basic 2+2+3+2+2 pattern, expands it, and adds a cross accent. Later the same pulse gets 7 notes in place of 11.
parameters: 3 states of one pulse: 11 notes; 11 notes with an accent on each third note; 7 notes
where: Against the Fall of Night (title track)

item: Change of feel on the way to the end
content: A piece can change its subdivision family near the end: a quintuplet groove gives way to a triplet feel. The album close uses metric modulations and changes of feel under a steady piano and string harmony.
parameters: 5 notes per beat, then 3 notes per beat
where: Paydushko Horo; Clock of the Long Now

item: Live versions are longer
content: The slots of the pieces in the big band film are longer than the studio tracks. The slots include talk, so the ratios are upper limits.
parameters: Slot against studio length: Cool 7 6:17 / 4:31 (1.39); Macchina 6:24 / 3:44 (1.71); Skrontch 5:54 / 4:54 (1.20); Hot Saturn 4:00 / 3:24 (1.18); Threshold 4:45 / 4:15 (1.12); Thicc 3:18 / 3:48 (0.87); All These People 5:08 / 3:52 (1.33); Drunk 7:06 / 3:26 (2.07). Median 1.27. Drunk live single: 4:31 (1.31)
where: Sungazer Plus concert film 2025 (computed from the time stamps)

item: New arrangement for each line-up
content: The same pieces are played by a quartet with keys, a quartet with guitar, and a big band. In 2022 the band also played its own changed arrangement of a meme track, with its tour manager on sax.
parameters: 3 line-up types for one repertoire

item: Contrast between sections
content: Neely's rule for arrangements: 'the more you contrast between A and B, the more like whole it feels'. Build in layers: start small, then add bass and drums, then guitar.
parameters: Maximum contrast between section A and section B

item: All players learn all parts
content: Each player learns the bass line, the chords, and the melody from the demo, by ear, with no charts. The band first plays the demo exactly. Then the players change the parts and the roles: "we earn the right to change things".
parameters: League: charts would limit rhythm, feel, and chord voicings. The sheet music is written after the album

item: A tune changes in rehearsal
content: Bet: on day 1 the groove was funk with the snare on beats 2 and 4. On day 6 it was Brazilian, with the low sound on 2 and 4 and a pandeiro. The solo went from guitar to a different instrument. The band also tried different tempos and keys.
parameters: 6 days from the first version to the last version

item: The same cycle in a new key
content: Thing of Gold: the melody and its 5 chords return 5 times. Each return is in a different key; one return has small changes.
parameters: 6 statements of 1 cycle in 6:25

item: Tracks get longer in concert
content: Concert length divided by album length: While We're Young 2.8; Shofukan 1.85; Sleeper 1.72; Tarova 1.70; Bad Kids to the Back 1.45; Bigly Strictness 1.10; Chonks 1.08; Even Us 1.06; Xavi 1.00.
parameters: Median 1.45 (derived). Shofukan in concert ends with a sing-along and a percussion jam
where: Live at the Royal Albert Hall (2019)

item: A different solo on each recording
content: Lingus: the solo is at the end of the tune, and a different member takes it on each recording. In a concert of 2015 trumpet and tenor sax traded solos, a second tenor sax played the last solo alone, and then the band went to a house feel. The 2024 edition of We Like It Here has all 8 tracks again as alternate takes.
parameters: 2 released takes of each of the 8 tracks
where: Lingus; We Like It Here (2024 edition)

item: The chorus is slower each time
content: In a solo song by League in 6/4, the tempo of the chorus is slower each time the chorus returns. A different song has a percussion groove in 5/4.
parameters: The tempo goes down one step at each return of the chorus

item: Motifs move through the ensemble
content: League wrote motifs and moved them to different parts of the orchestra; they continue through the full piece. His image: a face changes again and again, but the person stays the same.
parameters: Same motif; a new instrument at each return
where: As You Are But Not As You Were (Somni)

item: Loop varied; repetition
content: The one-bar loop changes in length and in order. Rests are added. Then it moves around the kit and inside the bar.
parameters: He names repetition "one of the most powerful tools". Terms: "proactive repetition", "coincidental interaction"

item: Larger versions of small songs
content: He arranges his songs for big band and for orchestra.
parameters: "F it Up" arrangement: about 1.5 hours of writing. "Doing the Things" grew from extra material of "Bank Account". Studio 138 BPM against live band 144 BPM ("Overtime")

item: Duo set for a larger band
content: The duo material is arranged for a nine-piece band.
parameters: Arranged by Robert "Sput" Searight: 3 saxophones or flutes, 2 guitars, bass, percussion, 2 keyboards, with the duo

item: Live version from the studio set
content: He mutes the drums and the parts with no pitch, then plays as much of the rest as he can.
parameters: The remainder is a backing track. About 4 days to set up and 1 week to learn

item: New pitches on a fixed rhythm
content: The rhythm of a riff stays and the pitches change. If the pitch set and the attack set have different sizes, the order shifts on each repeat.
parameters: 'Stengah' riff C: the rhythm of riff B with 4 pitches against 5 attacks. Riff I: the second phrase swaps two pairs of pitches. Riff D: the first note changes on the repeat. 'Pineal Gland Optics': 8 pitches against 14 attacks, in line again after 56 attacks

item: Half-step shift
content: The same riff returns one half step higher for more weight or more tension.
parameters: Riff I is riff H one half step higher (climax). The opening of riff B is one half step above its root. A verse can sit one half step below the riff before it

item: New sound or feel for the same riff
content: A repeat changes the instruments or the drum feel and keeps the notes.
parameters: 'Stengah': first one guitar with a lo-fi sound, then the full band. 'Bleed': cymbals in quarter notes, then in eighth notes, then with the riff. 'To Negate': the motive first in half time, then in normal time with sixteenths on the hi-hat. For the voice, the drummer closes the hi-hat for a drier sound

item: Changed endings and rotation
content: A fragment repeats with a slightly different ending each time. A looping riff can start in the middle of its pattern, so the ear finds the true start later.
parameters: 'Nostrum': each second statement has three eighth notes near the end and not two. TesseracT 'Retrospect': a syncopated fragment of dotted eighth notes with a new ending each time. obZen: three 'rotated' riffs

item: Same melody, new group lengths or new backbeat
content: A melody returns with all groups made shorter, or the same line meets a new drum pattern.
parameters: Fives become fours: 5+5+7+5+5+5 to 4+4+5+4+4+4. A pattern of 32 sixteenths shrinks to 20. One phrase against a 12/8 backbeat, then against patterns in 4/8 and 3/8
where: The Grid; Vardavar; Song for Melan and Rafik

item: Staged changes inside a cycle
content: Small changes come at fixed repeats of the line, so the listener can follow the cycle.
parameters: 'Out of the Grid': the melody notes change after the fourth repetition; octave doubling only at the start of the cycle and at the fourth repetition. 'Etude No. 1': a new left-hand voice enters at bar 17 for eight bars

item: Place of the climax
content: The peak of a solo comes a little after the golden-ratio point.
parameters: 5 synthesizer solos: the peak comes soon after 0.618 of the length. Examples: bars 8-9 of 11; bars 37-38 of 42

item: Build of a keyboard solo
content: Density, register, and echo grow together.
parameters: The solo gets more intense from about 7:00 to 8:00 of a 13:10 track: tone clusters, chords that go up, changes of echo repeat time. Next solo from about 11:30. Tension by crescendo and more voices; release by long held chords (Wandering Spirit Song)
where: Ostinato (Suite for Angela); Wandering Spirit Song

item: One cell for a long piece
content: A figure of two notes or a short cell goes round the band for 18 minutes.
parameters: The Sun Myth (18 min): a figure of two notes, freely extended. Intercosmosis (18 min): a short cell passes through small groups, with solo horns and cued space chords between. The energy goes up and down; no steady rise

item: Tempo that rises
content: The tempo goes up during the track.
parameters: Night Passage: the track "keeps going faster" (Erskine). Chameleon: slow rise through the track and a faster return of the riff

item: Call and response between bass sounds
content: Make more than one bass sound. Let the sounds alternate, by cuts in the MIDI part or by slices of bounced audio.
parameters: "one sound will ask a question and the other will answer"; three variants of one patch: static, detuned, with a soft LFO

item: Number of bass sounds in a bar
content: The drop changes its sound many times in each bar.
parameters: 2 to 4 different sounds in a bar; each lasts 1/2 beat to 2 beats; a new sound on or after the snare on beat 3; a fill in bar 4 and in bar 8. Estimate

item: Drop in parts A, B, C
content: Each 8-bar part changes the sub pattern a little. The mid-bass chops come in only for some sections.
parameters: 3 parts of 8 bars

item: Change of speed, order and metre of a sample
content: He slows a sample down and then speeds it up. He cuts a sample into slices and plays the slices in a new order. He changes the metre of the source.
parameters: Slices of an eighth note ("Don't Cry"); half speed, or the effect of half speed ("Time: The Donut of the Heart"); a 6/8 source becomes a swung 4/4 ("Bye.")

item: Stutter that accelerates
content: The repeat gets shorter in steps. Curves that are not locked to note values give a speed-up or a slow-down.
parameters: 32nd, then 64th, then 128th; the stutter fills the space of one eighth or one 16th note at the start or at the end of a bar

item: Most notes of a bebop solo belong to a repeated pattern
content: 82.6% of the notes begin a 4-interval pattern that occurs again in the corpus. 57.6% begin a pattern of intervals and rhythm. A pattern is repeated 26.3 times on average. The longest pattern has 49 intervals.
parameters: Interval patterns cover 0.83 of the notes; interval-and-rhythm patterns 0.58

item: Pattern coverage of a postbop tenor solo
content: 64.8% of the tones are in an interval pattern of six or more tones that occurs at least twice in his seven solos (mean 56%). Against all postbop tenor solos the coverage is 80.7% (mean 78.3%). Exact pitch patterns: 46.8% (mean 40.6%).
parameters: Own interval patterns 0.56 to 0.65; style patterns 0.78 to 0.81; exact pitch patterns 0.41 to 0.47

item: Long patterns are transposed, not repeated at pitch
content: Interval patterns of eight or more tones that occur at least twice: 77 for Hubbard and 125 for Shaw. Hubbard almost never repeats a long pattern that sounds similar. Shaw plays one pattern of 13 intervals in two solos.
parameters: Reuse the interval shape; change the pitch level, rhythm and metric position

item: One unit in four varies an earlier unit
content: About one quarter of the units (mean 25.1%, SD 15.3%) have a motivic relation to a preceding unit. A chain of related units has a mean length of 2.8 (SD 1.4). The share differs between performers but not between styles.
parameters: P(variation of an earlier unit) = 0.25; chain length 2 to 4

item: The accent pattern repeats; the timing repeats much less
content: The hi-hat amplitudes follow a pattern of high, low, medium, low, with 'very high' on the snare beats. Bars correlate 0.88 in amplitude but only 0.48 in timing. Odd bars correlate with odd bars at 0.93: the phrase has two bars.
parameters: Dynamics: fixed 2-bar template (r 0.9); timing: half template, half new (r 0.5)
where: Jeff Porcaro, 'I Keep Forgettin'', first ten bars

item: The swing ratio varies inside a piece
content: The SD of the swing ratio inside one piece is 0.32 to 0.58 around means of 1.57 to 2.11.
parameters: Ratio SD 0.3 to 0.6 inside a piece

item: Density changes from phrase to phrase
content: The event density of the phrases in one solo goes from 2.05 to 13.42 tones per second. In a Hubbard solo the density rises over the solo and falls at the end.
parameters: Phrase density range 2 to 13 notes/s inside one solo
where: Case study in the Jazzomat book
